title: Unity in the Church
definition: Unity in the Church is the Spirit-created oneness believers share in Christ and are called to preserve through truth, love, humility, and peace.
summary: The Church is called to live as one body under Christ.
christFocus: Jesus prayed for the unity of His people and reconciles believers to God and one another through His cross.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Unity in the Church is created by the Spirit, grounded in the Gospel, and centered on Christ. Believers are one body with one Lord, one faith, one baptism, and one God and Father.

Biblical unity is not uniformity or compromise of truth. It is shared life under Christ marked by humility, patience, love, forgiveness, sound doctrine, and mutual care.

The Church's unity is a witness to the world. Division, pride, and favoritism distort that witness, while Gospel unity displays the reconciling power of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Churches can be fractured by pride, preference, bitterness, favoritism, or secondary disputes. Unity matters because Christ has made His people one body and calls them to preserve that unity in love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pursue unity by practicing humility, forgiveness, patience, and truth. Refuse gossip and favoritism. Ask how your words and actions either build up or divide the body.
